page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-56 is a compute-optimized instance from the c2d family. It features 56 vCPUs mapped to 28 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 112.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core (82,135.96) and Geekbench multi-core (16,758.0). Memory performance is highly competitive, with a top-tier Passmark memory score (3,104.05) and strong small-block cached read bandwidth of 3,817.65 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidths remain average. Computational capabilities are further highlighted by strong results in software compilation (41,115.0 in Geekbench clang), ray tracing, and image processing.

Given its high vCPU count and dedicated compute resources, the c2d-highcpu-56 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It excels in database operations, showing strong performance in Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations (61.68 million operations per second). It is also well-suited for multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and moderate LLM inference tasks, particularly with smaller models.
